verses.zh: 愿你裂天而降；愿山在你面前震动―
verses.en: (63:19b)[NOTE:1] If only you would tear apart the sky[NOTE:2] and come down!The mountains would tremble[NOTE:3] before you!
notes: In BHS the chapter division occurs in a different place from the English Bible: 64:1 ET (63:19b HT) and 64:2-12 (64:1-11 HT). Beginning with 65:1 the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.
Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.

Or “quake.” נָזֹלּוּ (nazollu) is from the verbal root זָלַל (zalal, “quake”; see HALOT 272 s.v. II זלל). Perhaps there is a verbal allusion to Judg 5:5, the only other passage where this verb occurs. In that passage the poet tells how the Lord’s appearance to do battle caused the mountains to shake.
verses.commentary:
64:1 The first two lines are labeled as Isa. 63:19 in the MT. There is a series of PERFECT VERBS
from Isa. 64:18 through Isa. 64:19.

YHWH, who lives on high, "rends" (Qal PERFECT, BDB 902, KB 1146,
cf. Isa. 34:4; Rev. 6:14) the atmosphere of the earth (i.e. heavens, cf. Gen. 1:1).

As the creator approaches the creation quakes (Niphal PERFECT,
BDB 272, KB 272 [this form occurs only here and Jdg. 5:5, which is Deborah's praise/psalm of the defeat of
Hazor and its army], cf. Isa. 64:2; Ps. 18:7-15; 68:8; 77:18; 144:5)

For "heavens" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN.

verses.zh: 好像火烧干柴，又像火将水烧开，使你敌人知道你的名，使列国在你面前发颤！
verses.en: (64:1) As when fire ignites dry woodor fire makes water boil,let your adversaries know who you are,[NOTE:1] and may the nations shake at your presence!
notes: Heb “to make known your name to your adversaries.” Perhaps the infinitive construct with preposition לְ (lamed) should be construed with “come down” in v. 1a, or subordinated to the following line: “To make known your name to your adversaries, let the nations shake from before you.”
verses.commentary:
64:2 "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ Notice the purpose of YHWH is that His name be known and that the nations tremble
(hopefully in repentance, cf. Ps. 99:1-5; Jer. 33:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 你曾行我们不能逆料可畏的事。那时你降临，山岭在你面前震动。
verses.en: When you performed awesome deeds that took us by surprise,[NOTE:1] you came down, and the mountains trembled[NOTE:2] before you.
notes: Heb “[for which] we were not waiting.”
See the note at v. 1.
verses.commentary:
64:3

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB
"awesome things"

TEV
"terrible things"

NJB
"unexpected miracles"

JPSOA
"wonders"

LXX
"glorious deeds"

Peshitta
"wonderous things"

The Hebrew word (BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE) literally
means "fear," but in this form it can denote the majestic, awesome miracles of YHWH on behalf of Israel
(cf. Deut. 10:21; 2 Sam. 7:23; 1 Chr. 17:21; Ps. 66:3,5-6; 106:22; 145:6).

In Ps. 139:14 several Hebrew words are used in parallel.

- BDB 431 ‒ fearful

- BDB 811 and 810 ‒ wonderful

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

verses.zh: 从古以来，人未曾听见、未曾耳闻、未曾眼见在你以外有甚么神为等候他的人行事。
verses.en: Since ancient times no one has heard or perceived,[NOTE:1] no eye has seen any God besides you,who intervenes for those who wait for him.
notes: Heb “from ancient times they have not heard, they have not listened.”
verses.commentary:
64:4 The interpretive question is to whom does the PRONOUN "they" refer.

- national Israel/Judah

- the faithful returnees (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses))

- the nations (cf. Isa. 64:2)

- #2 and #3 together

64:4 "ear. . .eye" The covenant people's rebellion was predicted by YHWH in Isa. 6:9-10. Paul seems to build on
this in 1 Cor. 2:9, but uses it in a positive sense.

▣ "a God besides you" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

▣ "Who acts. . ." The word is "works" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 793, KB 889).
This is the theological distinction between YHWH and the idols.

- They cannot see, hear, act, speak, but He can and does!

- He does not have a consort or a pantheon.

- He cannot be bribed.

▣ "the one who waits for Him" This describes the person of faith. He/she waits (Piel
PARTICIPLE, BDB 314, KB 313). This word has the connotation of "hoping, trusting, waiting"
for God (cf. Isa. 8:17; 30:18; Hab. 2:3).

Another root (BDB 875 I) is also translated "wait," but often not as theologically significant
(cf Isa. 25:9; 26:8; 33:2; 40:31; Ps. 25:3; 27:14; 37:34; 40:1; 130:5; Prov. 20:22).

verses.zh: 你迎接那欢喜行义、记念你道的人；你曾发怒，我们仍犯罪；这景况已久，我们还能得救吗？
verses.en: You assist[NOTE:1] those who delight in doing what is right,[NOTE:2] who observe your commandments.[NOTE:3] Look, you were angry because we violated them continually. How then can we be saved?[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “meet [with kindness].”
Heb “the one who rejoices and does righteousness.”
Heb “in your ways they remember you.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “look, you were angry, and we sinned against them continually [or perhaps, “in ancient times”] and we were delivered.” The statement makes little sense as it stands. The first vav [ו] consecutive (“and we sinned”) must introduce an explanatory clause here (see Num 1:48 and Isa 39:1 for other examples of this relatively rare use of the vav [ו] consecutive). The final verb (if rendered positively) makes no sense in this context—God’s anger at their sin resulted in judgment, not deliverance. One of the alternatives involves an emendation to וַנִּרְשָׁע (vannirshaʿ, “and we were evil”; LXX, NRSV, TEV). The Vulgate and the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa support the MT reading. One can either accept an emendation or cast the statement as a question (as above).
verses.commentary:
64:5 "You meet him who. . ." The VERB (Qal PERFECT,
BDB 803, KB 910) in this context denotes an encounter of/for fellowship and/or kindness.

Notice the kind of people YHWH "meets" with.

- him who rejoices in doing righteous

- him who remembers You in Your ways

▣

NASB
"We continued in them a long time

And shall we be saved?"

NKJV
"In these ways we continue

And we need to be saved"

NRSV
"Because you hid yourself we transgressed"

NJB
"now we persist in your ways and we shall be saved"

JPSOA
"We have been steeped in them from of old

And can we be saved?"

LXX
"therefore we went away"

The MT is uncertain. AB suggests an emendation involving two consonants which yields, "we have long been rebels" (p. 190).

▣ Lines 3-5 ask a pertinent question. Israel/Judah are covenant-breaking people. Can a
sinful people be "saved" (i.e. "delivered," BDB 446, KB 448)

- from the physical consequences of sin

- from the spiritual consequences of sin

I want to believe, "Yes, yes, yes" (cf. Isa. 64:8-9)! But only divine mercy and grace (this chapter
is a prayer for YHWH's intervention) can do it (recommended translation of UBS Text Project, p. 164). The
consequences of Genesis 3 are staggering and relentless.

However, in this context (i.e. Isa. 64:4-7) this verse is not redemptive but condemnatory
(Isa. 64:8-12 are a cry for mercy). Israel sinned in the past and the present. If this is to be accepted as the
meaning then the VERB "delivered" (ישׁע, BDB 446, KB 448,
Niphal IMPERFECT) must be changed to "and we were evil" (רשׁע,
BDB 957; LXX, NRSV, TEV).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 我们都像不洁净的人；所有的义都像污秽的衣服。我们都像叶子渐渐枯干；我们的罪孽好像风把我们吹去。
verses.en: We are all like one who is unclean,all our so-called righteous acts are like a menstrual rag in your sight.[NOTE:1] We all wither like a leaf;our sins carry us away like the wind.
notes: Heb “and like a garment of menstruation [are] all our righteous acts”; KJV, NIV “filthy rags”; ASV “a polluted garment.”
verses.commentary:
64:6-7 Notice the consequences of sin.

- all of us ‒ scope of the problem (cf. Rom. 3:9-18,23; 11:32; Gal. 3:22)

- unclean (BDB 379)

- our righteousness is a polluted garment (cloth of menstruation, BDB 723, cf. Lev. 15:19-24)

- wither (BDB 615, KB 663, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Isa. 1:30; 34:4) like a leaf

- the wind takes us away

- none call on the name of the Lord (i.e. worship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

YHWH reacts to this tragedy of a sinful covenant people, meant to promote and clarify His own character.

- He hid His face (cf. Isa. 1:15; 54:8; Deut. 31:18)

- He delivered us (MT, מוג, "melted," BDB 556, KB 555, an emendation to the root
מגו, "hand over," [BDB 171, KB 545 I], fits better) into the power (i.e. consequences) of our iniquities
(this is theologically parallel to Rom. 1:24,26,28!)

These verses serve as a petition of confession. There is no reason why YHWH should
forgive/forget, but He does (cf. Ps. 103:11-12; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; 55:6-7; Micah 7:19)! The new covenant is in view here (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). YHWH
will deal with them (i.e. Israel) and with all humans in a new way based on His character, His acts, His purposes,
and through His Son's actions and Spirit's drawing!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 并且无人求告你的名；无人奋力抓住你。原来你掩面不顾我们，使我们因罪孽消化。
verses.en: No one invokes[NOTE:1] your name,or makes an effort[NOTE:2] to take hold of you. For you have rejected us[NOTE:3] and handed us over to our own sins.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “calls out in”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “calls on.”
Or “rouses himself”; NASB “arouses himself.”
Heb “for you have hidden your face from us.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “and you caused us to melt in the hand of our sin.” The verb וַתְּמוּגֵנוּ (vattemugenu) is a Qal preterite second person masculine singular with a first person common plural suffix from the root מוּג (mug, “melt”). However, elsewhere the Qal of this verb is intransitive. If the verbal root מוּג (mug) is retained here, the form should be emended to a Polel pattern (וַתְּמֹגְגֵנוּ, vattemogegenu). The translation assumes an emendation to וַתְּמַגְּנֵנוּ (vattemaggenenu, “and you handed us over”). This form is a Piel preterite second person masculine singular with a first person common plural suffix from the verb מָגָן (magan, “hand over, surrender”; see HALOT 545 s.v. מגן and BDB 171 s.v. מָגָן). The point is that God has abandoned them to their sinful ways and no longer seeks reconciliation.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，现在你仍是我们的父！我们是泥，你是窑匠；我们都是你手的工作。
verses.en: Yet,[NOTE:1] Lord, you are our father.We are the clay, and you are our potter;we are all the product of your labor.[NOTE:2]
notes: On the force of וְעַתָּה (veʿattah) here, see HALOT 902 s.v. עַתָּה.
Heb “the work of your hand.”
verses.commentary:
64:8-12 This is a prayer of hope for YHWH to remember His covenant and not His children's sin.

- You are our Father (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD)

- You are the potter

- we are the work of Your hand (cf. Isa. 29:16; 45:9)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你不要大发震怒，也不要永远记念罪孽。求你垂顾我们，我们都是你的百姓。
verses.en: Lord, do not be too angry!Do not hold our sins against us continually.[NOTE:1] Take a good look at your people, at all of us.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “do not remember sin continually.”
Heb “Look, gaze at your people, all of us.” Another option is to translate, “Take a good look! We are all your people.”
verses.commentary:
64:9 There is a series of commands in the sense of prayer requests.

- do not be angry beyond measure ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 893, KB 1124) used
in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Isa. 54:7-8

- do not remember iniquity forever ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 269, KB 269) used
in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Isa. 43:25

- look, all of us are Your people ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 613, KB 661)

All of these are similar to Isa. 57:16-17; Ps. 103:8-14.

verses.zh: 你的圣邑变为旷野。锡安变为旷野；耶路撒冷成为荒场。
verses.en: Your chosen[NOTE:1] cities have become a wilderness;Zion has become a wilderness,Jerusalem,[NOTE:2] a desolate ruin.
notes: Heb “holy” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV, NLT); NIV “sacred.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
64:10-11 All of the VERBS are PERFECTS ("become" used
four times). They describe the complete destruction of YHWH's wrath.

- the cities of Palestine are a wilderness

- Jerusalem is desolate

- the temple burnt with fire (i.e. Babylon in 586 B.C. and Titus in A.D. 70)

- all Israel's precious things are in ruin

verses.zh: 我们圣洁华美的殿―就是我们列祖赞美你的所在被火焚烧；我们所羡慕的美地尽都荒废。
verses.en: Our holy temple, our pride and joy,[NOTE:1] the place where our ancestors praised you,has been burned with fire;all our prized possessions have been destroyed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “our source of pride.”
Or “all that we valued has become a ruin.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，有这些事，你还忍得住吗？你仍静默使我们深受苦难吗？
verses.en: In light of all this,[NOTE:1] how can you still hold back, Lord?How can you be silent and continue to humiliate us?
notes: Heb “because of these”; KJV, ASV “for these things.”
verses.commentary: 64:12 God's people cry out for restraint and compassion. Please, please, no more, they cry. Please come to us again!

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 64:1-7

1Oh, that You would rend the heavens and come down,

That the mountains might quake at Your presence-

2As fire kindles the brushwood, as fire causes water to boil-

To make Your name known to Your adversaries,

That the nations may tremble at Your presence!

3When You did awesome things which we did not expect,

You came down, the mountains quaked at Your presence.

4For from days of old they have not heard or perceived

by ear,

Nor has the eye seen a God besides You,

Who acts in behalf of the one who waits for Him.

5You meet him who rejoices in doing righteousness,

Who remembers You in Your ways.

Behold, You were angry, for we sinned,

We continued in them a long time;

And shall we be saved?

6For all of us have become like one who is unclean,

And all our righteous deeds are like a filthy garment;

And all of us wither like a leaf,

And our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.

7There is no one who calls on Your name,

Who arouses himself to take hold of You;

For You have hidden Your face from us

And have delivered us into the power of our iniquities.
